Attached: 1 image

I decided to try #emacs for my note-taking at college, as well #programming #csharp. While I expected it to be not good, I actually have been really enjoying it as my main text editor, and respect how comfortable the default packages are. Of course, I still had to install three other packages (being magit and markdown-mode), but other than that, the defaults have fulfilled my needs.

Note that while I still tend to use #markdown, I actually mainly use #orgmode for my note-taking. It integrates really well in Emacs, and I can just generate my little note into an HTML file to print off from org-mode directly rather than having to open a shell and use pandoc. I do have to remember some of the keybindings, especially when making bullet point lists, however.

In regards to actually writing C#, it's not even that bad. I enjoyed writing my code for my projects, although I tended to use the shell often to use `dotnet solution`. This isn't a pain point however, since eshell got the job done pretty well, all things considered. I just need to set up an LSP and I should be fully able to replace VSCodium for what I do.

I do want to raise that it is quite rough in some scenarios, notably when you DO have to use the shell. For example, `file://` links result in strange artifacts, very visible when running fastfetch in any built-in terminal for Emacs. This isn't a deal-breaker as I can always just... use GNOME Terminal. Maybe I'll have more critiques in time but its' likely solvable with search engines and the wonderful built-in help mode. That's all I really have to say at the moment.
